headline: High: Devin’s broad write/network privileges can collide with TREK’s shared MCP and secrets-bearing workspace, creating dangerous prompt, data, and action cascades.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, and shared integrations, while TREK also exposes MCP and real-time collaboration. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if TREK content or shared artifacts are treated as trusted input. The pair is not documented directly, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Devin ingests TREK-generated text from MCP, files, or collaborative updates as instructions
IF TREK surfaces attacker-controlled content into a shared MCP or browser workflow
mitigations: Disable MCP connections between the agents for the session
Require explicit human approval before Devin follows any TREK-sourced instruction
Strip or label untrusted text in TREK outputs before handoff
Use separate workspaces and accounts for each agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens and has broad network egress; TREK handles API keys, MFA secrets, and reservation data. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive travel and engineering data can leak through Devin’s outbound integrations. The profiles show enough overlap to treat this as dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Devin can read TREK files, logs, or uploads in the same workspace
IF Devin forwards copied TREK content to GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, or other external services
mitigations: Place the agents in separate OS accounts or containers
Remove secrets from shared folders before any handoff
Block Devin from accessing TREK logs, uploads, and database exports
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets after shared use
Use redacted summaries instead of raw files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad network egress; TREK is collaborative and stores mutable data plus secrets. If both touch the same repo, database, or integration-backed resources, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles support a real write-conflict pathway, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository, database, or shared files without locking
IF Devin commits or edits while TREK is simultaneously updating collaborative state
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only for shared resources
Use file locks or a single-writer queue
Separate git branches and require manual merge review
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor, and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK consumes Devin’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into reservations, budgets, or other downstream actions. Because both agents can act on generated content and the interaction is undocumented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF TREK uses Devin-generated plans, facts, or code without verification
IF Devin’s outputs are used to trigger bookings, edits, or other downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action-taking
Require TREK to verify Devin outputs against source data
Limit Devin to drafting only, not executing
Log provenance for every handoff between agents

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly touches reservations, email addresses, country visit history, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Devin has broad cloud integrations and handles secrets. If EU travel data or other regulated personal data flows into Devin’s third-party integrations without a DPA or residency controls, the compliance risk is substantial. The profiles do not prove a DPA, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF TREK data includes EU PII, reservation records, or country visit history
IF Devin sends that data to external SaaS integrations without contractual or residency controls
mitigations: Restrict shared data to non-PII summaries
Confirm a DPA and residency policy before transfer
Disable external integrations for regulated records
Redact email addresses, confirmation numbers, and visit history before handoff
Keep compliance-sensitive data inside TREK only
